 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed under Section 164 of the I.M.V. Act seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 03.03.2024 at about 11.35 to 11.45 p.m, while the deceased along with friends were traveling in a Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MM-5315, when they reached near Vasuvalli village, Belakavadi, B.G.Pura road,
Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District, the driver of the said Car drove it in a rash & negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and moved car towards the left side of the road and dashed against the tree and then took right and dashed to another tree.
Due to the said impact, car was fully damaged and consequent to which the deceased who was seated front side of the car died on the way to the hospital and other inmates have sustained injuries.

Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies and they have spent substantial amount towards medical expenses, transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
Further it is alleged that at the time of accident the deceased SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 was studying in PUC 2nd Year and they have spent huge amount for his education.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of car and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.1 admitted that he is the RC owner of the Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MM-5315 and was duly insured with the 1st respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is submitted that the driver of the vehicle also possess valid and effective DL.

Further denied all the allegation made in the petition and prayed to dismiss the Rajshekhar Alias Rajkumar vs Jagdishkumar H on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178289931/
2 petition.
4.

sentences.text: After service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement and contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 in respect of vehicle No.KA-02-MM-5315.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of sections 147, 150, 159, 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petitions.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03.03.2024 at about 11.35 to 11.45 p.m., near Vasuvalli village,
Belakavadi - B.G.Pura road, Malavalli Taluk, Mandya District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-02- MM-5315 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 15 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.

Perused the entire materials placed on record.

 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.2 : The evidence of PW.1 and police documents placed on record indicate that on 03.03.2024 an accident had taken place and on the next day a complaint was lodged against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MM- 5315.

sentences.text: Based on the complaint, the Belakavadi police registered the FIR and took-up investigation, during which they got examined the aforementioned car from the IMV Inspector.
Ex.P.3 is the IMV report wherein it is opined by the IMV Inspector that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicle.
Therefore the driver of the car did not have sufficient reason to cause the accident.
The fact that yet he caused it leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving the car rashly & negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet (Ex.P.5) against him for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337, 338 & 304(A) of IPC and u/s 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 cross examined PW.1 at length.
But nothing could be elicited from his mouth to disbelieve his evidence.
Moreover the respondents have not adduced contra evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners.
Therefore based on oral and documentary evidence, I hold that actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MM-5315 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE No.1 :
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed that he is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the younger brother of the deceased.
The documents i.e., Ex.P12 to 15 notarized copies of the Aadhaar cards of the petitioners and deceased placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024
Accordingly, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE No.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.61,00,000/- due to the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
It is the specific defence urged by the petitioners counsel that the deceased was aged about 21 years, studying II PUC at BBMP College, Bengaluru and he was bright and intelligent student.

Due to the accidental death the petitioners were put into great mental shock and agony and as such, he had a bright future and because of his ill-fated accident which has become the bolt from the blue for the family of the petitioners.
It is also vociferously urged that in twinkling of eye whole family structure of the family of the petitioners is demolished by this ill-fated accident.
Except Ex.P.15/SSLC Marks Card, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the Rajshekhar Alias Rajkumar vs Jagdishkumar H on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178289931/
4 deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.

sentences.text: Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2024.
It is trite SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 law that when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 year 2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

12. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card and SSLC Marks card of the deceased to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P13 & 15, wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 12.09.2003. which indicates that he was aged (20 years 5 months 21 days) 21 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '18'.
13.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 21 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident,
deceased aged about 21 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.23,100/- p.m. (Rs.16,500 + 6,600/- i.e. 40%).

14. Further as stated above that, deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenditure.

15. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,550/- p.m. and the multiplier '18' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.24,94,800/- (Rs.11,550 X 12 X 18) SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.24,94,800/- under the head of loss of dependency.

16. In this case, petitioner No.1 & 2 are the father and mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a daughter causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their daughter during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

17. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 consortium to be awarded.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
20. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of Insurance Policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,11,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the SCCH-23 MVC.5489/2024 compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 45% Petitioner No.2 - 45% Petitioner No.3 - 10% Out of the share amount of petitioners No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 25% each shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 5 years and the remaining 75% each shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
